A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAGE study. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original utility and privacy experiments on HealthCareMagic and Wiki-PII, together with model-choice, attribute-count, and retrieval-count ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds utility evaluations, stronger paraphrasing comparisons, direct leakage checks, and token-length and generation-cost results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same attribute-based generation followed by iterative privacy-agent and rewriting-agent refinement. The SAGE prompts and stopping procedure are retained; new paraphrasing comparators and domain-adaptation suggestions do not establish a changed SAGE method.

E1.justification: V2 adds PopQA to the evaluated QA datasets in Table 5 and examines full synthetic-data exposure as a worst-case scenario in A.5. Existing medical-dialog and Wiki-PII coverage remains. Financial applications are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 adds three stronger paraphrasing comparators in Tables 9–10: GPT-4o rewriting, GPT-4o with a generic privacy instruction, and GPT-4o with the detailed Joe privacy checklist. These substantially strengthen comparison against direct privacy-aware rewriting. Existing main-table comparators remain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces answer-occurrence EM and Ragas correctness evaluation, direct comparison of 100 synthetic/original samples, and paraphrasing comparisons labeled as using 100 prompts. These supplement the retained 250-prompt main attacks; the original splits, retrieval settings, and model defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test leakage directly from synthetic data (A.5), whether stronger single-pass privacy-aware paraphrasing suffices (A.6), and token-length and monetary costs (A.7). The original model, attribute-count, and retrieval-count ablations and synthetic examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Newly reported average costs, token lengths, and refinement rounds are descriptive results rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–5 retain their results. New Tables 5–10 add utility, leakage, and cost outcomes: for example, Table 5 reports NQ EM of 0.38 for Stage-2 versus 0.24 for original retrieval, while Table 8 reports targeted leakage counts of 0 for Wiki and 1 for HealthCareMagic. These are additional evaluations, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: A.8 adds standard ROUGE-L and BLEU-1 formula explanations. The privacy-upper-bound and differential-privacy discussions remain informal; no new theorem, proof, formal guarantee, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two-stage SAGE contribution, novelty positioning, and claim of maintaining retrieval utility while reducing privacy leakage. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets synthetic/original overlap as an extraction-risk upper bound, argues for advantages over stronger single-pass paraphrasing, and discusses inference-cost savings. Section 6 explicitly distinguishes empirical attack resistance from differential privacy, while A.10 adds domain-adaptation guidance and a domain-expertise limitation.

D1.justification: V2 adds paraphrasing prompt details, Ragas and metric documentation, token-counting and generation-cost information, and a GitHub code URL replacing the anonymous repository link. Core SAGE prompts and dataset-construction instructions are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. The paper retains its positioning relative to prior RAG privacy and synthetic-data methods; added evaluation-tool mentions do not revise that research relationship.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact, with local wording edits, clarifications, and new cross-references. The appendix gains metric explanations and application discussion, with existing material renumbered around the added subsections.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, six result tables and one prompt table are added, and main Tables 2–4 gain metric-direction arrows and layout adjustments. Existing appendix prompt and example tables are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's BLEU/ROUGE utility assessment and simpler paraphrasing baseline, v2 adds answer-oriented metrics and stronger privacy-aware comparisons. Cost reporting and clearer privacy qualifications also improve transparency. These gains are limited by sparse configuration details for the new evaluations and inconsistent Privacy/Joe labeling in Table 18.
